title: The Translatability of Tradition: Curating South Asian Heritage Lineages for Contemporary Architecture
dek: Which indigenous lineages carry the geometric rigour to leave the page and become permanent built surface, and which remain exploratory.
author: Preeti Padaley
authorBio: Founder & Principal Curator, Artha Indus Atelier. MBBS, MHSA, PMP.
imageAlt: Comparative study of South Asian heritage lineages assessed for architectural translatability.
excerpt: Authentic curatorial translation does not simply copy a heritage artform or painting onto a wall; it extracts the underlying geometric tension of the lineage and gives it structural resonance within modern space.

title: The Sūtra & the Senses: A Curatorial Inquiry into Visual Fluency, Ancient Morphology, and Built Space
dek: What visual neuroscience suggests about why ancestral geometries feel restful, and where the honest limits of that argument lie.
author: Preeti Padaley
authorBio: Founder & Principal Curator, Artha Indus Atelier. MBBS, MHSA, PMP.
imageAlt: Diagram relating the grammar of ancestral form, symmetry, grouping and fractal dimension, to built architectural surfaces.
excerpt: To examine Indian geometry through a neuroaesthetic lens is not to reduce sacred art to biology, but to explore how ancient visual masters intuitively calibrated form to the structural architecture of human perception.

title: Beyond the Paisley: Ancient Morphology, Architectural Materiality, and the Quiet Luxury of the Bīja
dek: The curved teardrop dismissed as “paisley” was never ornament. It is a germinating seed contour, and it carries architectural weight.
author: Preeti Padaley
authorBio: Founder & Principal Curator, Artha Indus Atelier. MBBS, MHSA, PMP.
imageAlt: Diagram titled The Morphology of the Bīja, charting the regional variants of the seed contour across Kashmir, Andhra Pradesh, Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan and Gujarat.
excerpt: Long before industrial looms flattened its geometry into two-dimensional novelty, the bīja was an architectural prayer, a concentrated nucleus of life holding immense kinetic energy within an asymmetric curve.

title: The Living Axis: Translating Zoomorphic and Botanical Lineages into Contemporary Architecture
dek: Five archetypal geometries, Vṛkṣa, Kūrma, Matsya, Mayūra and Āraṇya, recovered from decorative trivialisation and returned to architectural materiality.
author: Preeti Padaley
authorBio: Founder & Principal Curator, Artha Indus Atelier. MBBS, MHSA, PMP.
imageAlt: Curatorial diagram of the five archetypal South Asian geometries and their translation into architectural relief.
excerpt: In classical South Asian spatial thought, zoomorphic and botanical motifs were never decorative flourishes; they were structural equations balancing cosmic order against built space.

title: From Brushstroke to Bas-Relief
dek: Translating South Asian Heritage Lineages into Restorative Architecture
author: Preeti Padaley
authorBio: Founder & Principal Curator, Artha Indus Atelier. MBBS, MHSA, PMP.
imageAlt: Sweeping Himalayan Thangka celestial cloudscapes in sage green and liquid-gold linework across a curved wellness-spa sanctuary wall.
excerpt: When ancestral art moves beyond decoration, it ceases to sit passively on a wall; it becomes the architectural skin of the room, shaping light, sound, and emotional stillness.
